column9: The capability is a growable logical array: add(T) appends at the next index, get/set/pin address by long index. Values live in fixed-length pages. A page spills to a private scratch file (codec image, CRC32C, atomic move, bounded serialized size) and pages back in on access, under a page-count budget and sampled heap/physical headroom. A hot path samples once per 1,024 resident accesses; an admission transfers one cleared page container. Leases pin a page; close() deletes every file. No owner has this capability. M3ObjectResidency is a fixed-size int-slot arena: its slot count is final, it does not grow, it spills per slot through a caller SpillStore, it has no files, pages or index-addressed append, and its budget is bytes, not pages. Expressing the array on it would mean rewriting the donor, not relocating it. A MERGE would put a second storage model (growable pages, files) into it, giving two owners in one file. M3PagedLongArray and M3LongBigList hold primitives in heap only, with no codec, spill or leases. LazyObjectParent is a String-keyed proof of concept outside the reactor. #2566 called this "a third spill owner"; it is the spill owner of a different structure (an indexed append-only array), not of the slot arena or the keyed lazy parent.

It is the array's pressure seam: the public Probe interface (the array's constructor takes one; every donor test injects snapshots through it), a Snapshot with physical availability/total and physicalLow(min), runtime()/runtimeWithOptionalNative()/current()/describe(), and the optional JNI loader. M3RuntimeHeap owns the growth-capacity policy: Pressure NORMAL/WARM/HIGH, chooseCapacity and segmented amortization, no injection point, no physical evidence. EXTEND is excluded: M3RuntimeHeap is protected (com-synexia-22's), and a Probe/physical member there would change its public contract. Overlap: the heap fields are the same three Runtime reads in the same order (totalMemory, freeMemory, maxMemory) with the same used clamp; NEC row in RELOCATION_MAP.tsv, the donor body is kept and M3RuntimeHeap is not edited. Without libm3_residency, nativeAvailable() is false and every sample carries physical -1, -1: the donor's documented fallback, run by M3MemoryPressureSamplingTest mode java.

column9: Optional: M3MemoryPressure works without it, so this leaf does not need it. Its capability overlaps the JDK's container-aware memory metrics: Windows GlobalMemoryStatusEx, Linux /proc/meminfo, cgroup v1/v2 limit and usage. The deltas are memory.high tightening and the minimum over the cgroup ancestry (JDK 21 reads memory.max of the process's own cgroup only). Per "JDK owns fast implementations", the native leaf must first decide between EXTEND java.base platform metrics and ABSORB of the native code. The loader name m3_residency is kept in the relocated class as the seam for that leaf.
